# Complaints handling

How to Submit a Complaint

You can submit your complaint through any of the following channels for your convenience:

Email: Send details to complaints@leantech.me

Website: Fill in our online contact form 

Complaint Acknowledgment

All complaints will be acknowledged within one (1) working day of receipt.

Complaint Handling [...] Complaint Handling

All complaints will be investigated and resolved within five (5) working days from the date of receipt. If a complaint requires more time, the consumer will be notified of the reason for the delay and the revised timeline.

Complaint Escalation

Unresolved complaints after five (5) working days will be escalated internally and tracked until closure.

Inquiry or Escalation

If you wish to inquire about or escalate the outcome, you may contact us through the available communication channels.

results.content:
Title: The Joy of Broken Links: Embracing a Frustrating User Journey | AxureBoutique
Start typing to search the catalog. # The Joy of Broken Links: Embracing a Frustrating User Journey. Learn practical ideas and methods from this the joy of broken links: embracing a frustrating user journey article to improve product design, UX work, and Axure prototyping. In the world of user experience design, broken links are often seen as a nuisance, a frustrating roadblock that disrupts the seamless flow of a user's journey. However, what if we were to challenge this perspective and consider the joy that can be found in encountering broken links? This explores the idea of embracing a frustrating user journey and highlights the potential benefits it can bring to both users and designers. Perfection is often the goal in user experience design, but it can also lead to a sterile and predictable experience. Broken links introduce an element of unpredictability and imperfection, which can actually make the user journey more engaging and memorable. This sense of mystery and unpredictability can create a sense of joy and excitement in the user experience. For instance, imagine clicking on a broken link within a blog post that was supposed to lead to a related article. By embracing broken links, designers can encourage users to venture off the beaten path, fostering a sense of curiosity and discovery. A frustrating user journey can actually help build resilience in users. For example, encountering a broken link on a website's navigation menu might prompt users to utilize the search function or explore other sections of the site to find the desired information. By embracing broken links, designers can empower users to overcome challenges and develop valuable skills. By tracking and analyzing broken links, designers can identify patterns and address underlying issues in the user experience. By embracing broken links, designers gain a deeper understanding of the user's perspective and the challenges they face. This empathy can lead to more thoughtful and user-centric design decisions, ultimately enhancing the overall user experience. For example, if a designer encounters a broken link while testing a website, they can empathize with the user's frustration and work towards improving the navigation or error handling to provide a smoother experience.

# Broken links on county’s new website still frustrating many residents

By Matt Blitz

")

What appears when a broken link is clicked on Arlington County’s new website (via Arlington County)

Despite promising improved functionality, Arlington County’s new website launched last month remains riddled with broken links that are frustrating some residents.

Last month, Suzanne Smith Sundburg was preparing to make public comments at an upcoming Arlington County Planning Commission meeting. As someone who is a passionate about weighing in on local issues, she uses the county website often for research and updates on county happenings. [...] Last week, Sundburg wrote an open letter to county officials expressing her displeasure about this missing information.

“This revamp of the county website has been akin to the burning down of a library with half of the books still inside,” she wrote. “In this case, the ‘books’ still exist — the community simply has no access to them.”

County officials acknowledge the issues and say they’re working on it, noting the broken links are a result of issues migrating from the old site to the new site. [...] Sundburg isn’t the only one who has noticed a number of dead-end links. ARLnow has received a tips in recent weeks from other users who have encountered broken links preventing them from accessing county webpages, documents and information, such as information on how to pay a parking ticket or the county’s Community Energy Plan.

“The Arlington County revised website is horribly broken, with links that don’t work,” said one anonymous tipster. “It’s a travesty.”

The Lyon Village Civic Association says it is still working with the county to update all the county links on its own website.

“We have asked the County webmaster to get these reestablished, some have, but not all,” it said in a recent post.
